findings.title: Current Admin sales management lacks canonical mutation authorization and API contracts
findings.observed_contract: Current FRs and pages require Entry and Karaoke sales-condition mutations, but the current capability matrix and API catalog do not define the contract. Listed capabilities and routes are proposals in an unmerged UCR only.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Two distinct admin capabilities, exact operation IDs and routes, Zod schemas, authorization, current-state conflict behavior, and idempotency are missing from the current canonical contract.
findings.why_this_matters: Implementers would have to invent authority and mutation semantics.
findings.system_impact: Admin sales operations cannot be securely implemented with Hono authority.
findings.implementation_impact: Canonicalize two distinct admin capabilities in SPEC-060, then define exact operations in SPEC-110 and propagate them.
findings.test_impact: Capability, route, schema, conflict, idempotency, audit, observability, and acceptance tests cannot bind to current contracts.
findings.acceptance_impact: Required Admin mutation behavior cannot be demonstrated without guessed APIs.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: First canonicalize the two capabilities in SPEC-060; then add exact operation IDs/routes/Zod schemas/auth/current-state conflict/idempotency in SPEC-110 and update dependent specs, tests, observability, and acceptance. Do not implement UCR-proposed endpoints pre-incorporation.

findings.title: Current Goods Handoff operational UI lacks API contracts and resolution ownership is cyclic
findings.observed_contract: Current staff preview and Admin list/detail/allowed-command behavior cannot be implemented. The UCR limits commands to the range allowed by SPEC-030 and SPEC-060, but neither enumerates the actual Admin command semantics.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Exact permitted Admin operation semantics and safe HTTP command/read schemas are missing; resolution ownership is cyclic until semantics are enumerated.
findings.why_this_matters: Handoff is operationally sensitive and may be irreversible.
findings.system_impact: Unsafe handoff transitions or implementation-by-guesswork are possible.
findings.implementation_impact: SPEC-130 must define exact permitted Admin operation semantics, followed by SPEC-110 command contracts.
findings.test_impact: Authorization, transition, confirmation, idempotency, and failure-path tests lack canonical operations.
findings.acceptance_impact: Safe handoff behavior and minimal PII preview cannot be accepted end to end.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: SPEC-130 specifies exact permitted admin semantics, not a generic state editor; SPEC-110 adds exact safe HTTP commands/read schemas. Staff preview may be added independently while preserving minimal PII response.

findings.title: Current Admin filter and authoritative-read pages lack canonical API query/read contracts
findings.observed_contract: General cursor and allowlist rules exist, but operation query names/types and current Admin detail/read APIs are absent.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Canonical allowlisted query schemas and public-reference-safe read operations are missing from the current API catalog.
findings.why_this_matters: A client-filtered or invented query cannot guarantee authoritative current state or safe reload behavior.
findings.system_impact: Admin views cannot safely retrieve and confirm current data.
findings.implementation_impact: SPEC-110 must add exact query and read operations to the existing catalog.
findings.test_impact: Query validation, pagination, filtering, authorization, and authoritative-read tests cannot target current operation contracts.
findings.acceptance_impact: Filter, detail, reload, and confirmation acceptance scenarios remain unimplementable.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: Add exact Zod allowlist query schemas and public-reference-safe read operations to SPEC-110; preserve current filter semantics and capabilities, do not substitute public APIs, and update DB/security/observability/test/acceptance dependencies. Do not implement UCR examples before incorporation.

findings.title: Current API routes without Operation IDs violate current observability and acceptance contracts
findings.observed_contract: SPEC-170 permits fallback method/path/capability behavior tests, while observability requires exact SPEC-110 API-* IDs and every server operation to have a bounded operation ID. Unique IDs are currently UCR-only.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Current API routes lack unique canonical Operation IDs.
findings.why_this_matters: Logs, audit records, metrics, and acceptance evidence cannot reliably identify operations.
findings.system_impact: Required observability and correlation semantics cannot be met.
findings.implementation_impact: SPEC-110 must assign unique API-* identifiers without changing routes and propagate them downstream.
findings.test_impact: Operation-ID correlation and observability tests cannot assert canonical identifiers.
findings.acceptance_impact: Observability acceptance fails for current routes.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: Assign unique API-* identifiers in SPEC-110 without changing routes, then propagate to tests, logs, audits, metrics, and manifests. A security/observability owner change would require a separate contract change. Never invent IDs downstream.

findings.title: Current manual recovery contract cannot be completed through canonical Hono API
findings.observed_contract: Current manual recovery runbooks require dedicated operation-specific recovery APIs, but the current catalog provides read-only or limited mutations and no canonical commands for result reconciliation or re-evaluation. Proposed commands remain UCR-only.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Operation-specific fixed-precondition recovery commands are missing from the canonical Hono API.
findings.why_this_matters: Unknown external results cannot be safely reconciled by generic state mutation.
findings.system_impact: Payment, refund, and email recovery can leave production state unresolved or unsafe.
findings.implementation_impact: SPEC-110 must canonicalize recovery commands at the application boundary.
findings.test_impact: Recovery, authorization, cause/key, idempotency, audit, and result-reconciliation tests cannot target current commands.
findings.acceptance_impact: Reliability and manual recovery acceptance cannot pass.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: Canonicalize operation-specific fixed-precondition commands in SPEC-110, retaining cause, key, current authority, authorization, and audit constraints and forbidding generic state changes; then propagate the contract. Do not introduce UCR routes alone.

findings.title: Additional Admin operational indexes require query-plan-based canonicalization
findings.observed_contract: Core indexes exist; the UCR proposes future pattern indexes, but no current data volume, SLO, or test evidence establishes that the current FR is unimplementable.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Named future indexes and supporting query-plan evidence are not yet canonicalized.
findings.why_this_matters: Operational filters could degrade as data volume grows.
findings.implementation_impact: Do not add speculative indexes before query evidence exists.
findings.test_impact: Future performance/index tests should follow accepted query plans.
findings.acceptance_impact: No current acceptance blocker; performance evidence is a later prerequisite.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: Retain as a nonblocking UCR; after associated APIs are accepted, use real query plans and selectivity to decide named indexes and tests.

findings.title: Additional recovery-page wiring is dependent clarification, not independently current-blocking
findings.observed_contract: Generic current recovery link/action UI dynamically applies only where an explicit upstream operation exists; new dedicated operations are blocked by REV-005.
findings.conflicting_or_missing_contract: Dedicated recovery-page wiring for newly canonicalized operations is not yet specified.
findings.why_this_matters: Detail-page recovery actions could expose operations without the correct precondition or capability handling.
findings.system_impact: Recovery UI wiring remains unspecified after the API contract changes.
findings.implementation_impact: Wire only accepted recovery operations after UCR-150-001 is incorporated.
findings.test_impact: UI tests must bind each action to current precondition, capability, confirmation, and result contracts.
findings.acceptance_impact: Baseline recovery page behavior exists; dedicated wiring is a dependent follow-up.
findings.recommended_resolution_direction: Incorporate UCR-150-001 into SPEC-110 first, then wire only those operations with current precondition, capability, confirmation, and result handling; never add a generic recovery button.
